title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for hyperglycemia.

HPI
The patient is a 58-year-old male presenting for a follow-up visit regarding his type 2 diabetes. He reports that his blood glucose levels have been poorly controlled over the last month despite consistent adherence to his medication regimen. He notes increased thirst and frequent urination. He has been on long-term treatment involving both an oral hypoglycemic and insulin. He denies any recent changes to his activity level or significant illnesses.

Medication List
- Metformin 1000mg BID
- Insulin glargine and Lispro as directed

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented. Skin is intact with no acute lesions. Vital signs are stable. No acute distress noted.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus
2. Hyperglycemia

Plan
The patient will continue his current regimen of metformin and insulin. We will monitor his glucose levels closely over the next two weeks. The patient was instructed to record his daily readings and return for a follow-up appointment in one month to evaluate the effectiveness of the current management plan.
explanations: Diabetes documented as poorly controlled, out of control, or with hyperglycemia is coded to diabetes with hyperglycemia.
When both insulin and oral hypoglycemics are used, assign both Z79.4 and Z79.84.

distractors.why: Hyperglycemia is a complication with its own code.
Both Z codes are assigned when both drug types are used.
